title: Shadow-tiling cohort convergence + rollback-oracle integration
author: Aisha Rahman
release_notes: Adds shadow-tiling cohort convergence algorithm and a heuristic rollback oracle. No API-breaking changes. Operators can enable via rollout.spec.shadowTiling and tune convergence.window.
description:
Motivation: As we run more shadow traffic experiments at scale, individual cohorts that overlap (by user, session or feature flag) create noisy signals that delay safe promotions. This PR introduces 'shadow-tiling' — a deterministic tiling scheme that partitions shadow traffic into cohort-convergent slices and wires a rollback-oracle that recommends automated short-circuit rollbacks if multi-signal divergence is detected.

What this PR does: - Introduces a server-side deterministic tiling algorithm which maps incoming requests into shadow tiles based on a convergent hash (combining user_id, country, and experiment_salt). Tiles are stable under resharding and respect session affinity. - Adds a cohort convergence evaluation step to the rollout controller: each tile reports metric deltas (latency, error rate, quality regressions), and the controller aggregates with outlier-resistant statistics (median-of-means) per-cohort. - Implements a rollback-oracle that watches multi-metric divergence patterns and recommends / auto-applies short rollbacks when configured. The oracle uses a simple credit system so transient spikes don't cause oscillation. - Adds observability surfaces: per-tile metrics, convergence score, oracle decisions, and a replayable audit trail for post-mortem. - Exposes rollout.spec.shadowTiling.{enabled,shard_count,convergence_window,credit_budget,auto_rollback} in the API and documents defaults.

Checklist: - [x] Core tiling + mapping implemented in rollout controller and router layer - [x] Aggregation & median-of-means implementation with unit tests - [x] Rollback-oracle with config and safety credits - [x] Console dashboard panels and telemetry hooks - [x] Backwards-compatible API additions (feature-gated) - [x] End-to-end smoke test against the perf-canary harness

Compatibility notes: The changes are additive. Existing rollouts remain unchanged unless shadowTiling is enabled. We ship a default conservative budget for auto_rollback=false in order to let operators adopt slowly.

Related: ENG-3124 (cohort signalling improvements), ENG-4198 (rollback automation roadmap).

review_conversation: Marco Li (2026-02-26): This looks promising. Two quick asks: (1) can we document the failure modes where tiles might skew due to upstream ID hashing changes? (2) add a small simulation in tests that shows the credit-burnback behavior over repeated spikes?
Aisha Rahman (2026-02-26): Added docs section and a new simulation test (tests/e2e/shadow_tiling_smoke_test.go) that replays bursts to validate the credit logic. See latest commit 1b9c3da.

Dana Ortiz (2026-03-01): Ran the perf-canary with 10k req/s mix. Router changes added ~0.6ms median p50 on shadow-enabled paths — acceptable but please ensure the console highlights when shadow-tiling is enabled to avoid operator surprises.

Aisha Rahman (2026-03-01): Moved a small part of the tile computation off the hot path (memoized per-session) which reclaimed ~0.4ms. Noted in changelog and UI shows a badge when shadow-tiling is active.

Priya Singh (2026-03-03): Security quick review: proto additions look fine. Confirmed no additional scope for PII collection; tile key uses a salted hash only. Approving once we add the audit trail TTL config.
Aisha Rahman (2026-03-03): Added auditTrail.ttl to API (docs updated), and a migration note for existing audits. Marking as ready for squash-merge.
notes_on_deployment: Staged rollout recommended: enable shadowTiling in a single region with auto_rollback=false for 48 hours and watch convergence.score and oracle.credit_usage. Increase shard_count gradually if per-tile sample sizes are low.
